correctness.rationale: In characteristic two the diagonal identity gives P(x)^2=0. In this algebra (x0+x1t+x2t²)^2=x0²+x1²t², so the image lies in kt². Write P(t²)=ct²; the pair (1,t²) gives 0=P(ct²)=c²t², so c=0. Conversely for the proposed maps both the product on the left and P applied to the right argument vanish: the image ideal has square zero and is killed by P. This proves the classification for each finite characteristic-two field, including F₂, and gives rank at most one and P²=0. An automorphism has t↦ut+vt², u≠0, and t²↦u²t². On conjugating, the t² term of the inverse image of t contributes zero, giving (a,b)↦(u²a,ub). Normalize b to one when nonzero, retaining a/b²; on b=0,a≠0 the finite field square map is bijective. The effective scaling has trivial stabilizer on each nonzero pair, so q+2 classes and q−1 elements per nonzero orbit, including singleton orbits when q=2. This symbolic proof establishes all claims; the frozen small-field enumeration and F₃ contrast were inspected as recorded corroboration, not executed or used as the proof.
